gaps.sentence: Air ___ has become much cheaper in the last twenty years.
gaps.hint: uncountable noun for travelling in general
gaps.explanation: 'Air travel' is the fixed expression for travelling by plane; 'travel' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: Should any dispute ___, the matter will go to arbitration.
gaps.explanation: 'Arise' = (problems, disputes) occur; 'rise' means go up and 'raise' needs an object.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: He ___ all knowledge of the missing file.
gaps.explanation: 'Deny all knowledge of something' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: This small car is very ___ to run.
gaps.explanation: 'Economical' means costing little or saving money; 'economic' relates to trade, industry or the economy.
'It's' is short for 'it is' or 'it has'; here it means 'it has been raining'. The possessive is 'its'.
